system.summary: Telegraphic code of five-digit groups over 10000-99999 with a short group '03'; words and syllables (the decoder writes 'Po-des', 'Ros-a'); not alphabetical (ter 38564, com 58215).
system.sibling_key: The code Sabugosa used in May 1903 (targets/sabugosa1910) is a different, alphabetical code with groups up to 23400.
system.notes: distinct_symbols = distinct items seen in the three telegrams (60, '03' included). key_order 'random' rests on two inferred values only (ter 38564, com 58215), which run against alphabetical order. The three telegrams share groups (10734, 43554, 78341; 58215, 91518), so they use one code.

prior_solution.where: Decodes of the time filed with the telegrams: on m0058 itself (French) and on the Hotel Bristol card m0060 (decode of m0054). No printed decipherment found (one web search).

conditions.human_role: WAINUT chose the catalogue items and set the rules; AI language-model agents fetched the images, transcribed, compared the decodes and checked the work. No hand correction of readings recorded.
tools: groups.py (group counts, repeats, shared groups, chance control, letter-for-digit control)
models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT); a vision-capable language model for the transcription

solution.what: All 61 images of M12 fetched through the DigitArq JSON backend (the record says not accessible, but the images download). Telegrams on m0054-55, m0056-57, m0058-59.
Transcribed the three telegrams: 14, 47 and 13 items; headers and stamps read.
m0058 carries its own decode of the time in French under the code groups; transcribed and translated.

Independent re-reading: m0058 confirmed digit for digit. Corrected the first pass: m0054 runs Lisbon -> Paris (the form's rule puts the serial number after the place of origin) and is dated 12 May 1903 by the stamp CENTRAL PARIS 12 MAI 03.

m0058: the 60 digits against the 60 letters of the decode give 37 conflicts, shuffled digits 38.1 on average: a code, not a letter cipher. Random 12- and 44-group telegrams share two groups in under 1 of 20,000 trials, so the shared groups mean one code.

Found the card m0060 (Hotel Bristol, Paris): the clear words of m0054 with a Portuguese sentence in place of the 14 groups, i.e. the decode of m0054. The two repeated groups (38564 at 5 and 11, 58215 at 7 and 13) sit where 'ter ... com' repeats in the decode, which fixes ter, combinado, com and fallado.

m0056 (4 Mar 1903, 47 items) has no decode; tried the values from m0054 and m0058. Only 58215 (com) recurs with a value; the groups it shares with m0058 (10734, 43554, 78341) get no value because the m0058 decode does not align one to one.

One web search: no printed decipherment of these telegrams. Related pointer only: A. H. Norris, BHS Portugal Report 4 (1977) p. 56, on a letter of Queen Amélie to Manuel II with words in cipher given in brackets (a different document).

texts.label: m0054, Lisbon -> Paris, 12 May 1903
texts.summary: King Carlos thanks the Queen, then in Paris, for her telegram and says all is well; in code he tells her she may give [something] but only after arranging it with Rosa (probably the Portuguese minister in Paris) and after the French government has been spoken to. The children kiss her hand.

reading_review.by: WAINUT (AI language-model agent, checked against the images)
reading_review.note: The decode on m0060 is a complete Portuguese sentence framed by the telegram's own clear French words; no holes. The object of 'dar' is not stated in the text.

texts.label: m0058, undated (spring 1903?)
texts.summary: King Carlos tells the Queen that all are well, that he has written to her at Malta, and sends his love and the children's greetings. Fits her Mediterranean cruise of spring 1903.

reading_review.by: WAINUT (AI language-model agent, checked against the image)
reading_review.note: Telegraphic French from the decode of the time; 'salue' is singular as written; two readings of the last clause are given in the translation.

texts.label: m0056, Lisbon -> Tlemcen, 4 Mar 1903
texts.summary: Code telegram of 86 taxed words to Queen Amélie on board the yacht Amélie at Oran; no decode found.
texts.note: Not decoded: one group (58215) has an inferred value from m0054. Shown so that others can work on it.

outcome.notes: Contributed by WAINUT (catalogue 401). The archive says some documents are in cipher; the letters (French, from King Carlos, 1904-1905) are in clear, and only the three telegrams are coded. The Hotel Bristol card m0060 was not noticed in the first pass; it was found while checking the contact sheets for this pull request and was re-read once more against the image by a reviewing agent, who agrees with the transcription.
